issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI workaround into core/setup.py runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: The pin exists because mmcv 2.1.0's build imports pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removes. That's a CI build-time problem. Putting setuptools<82 in core/setup.py forces every downstream autogluon user to accept the cap indefinitely. Scope it to the CI scripts where the FIXME already lives, not the library's runtime dependencies.

issues.description: mmdet silently bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no justification.
issues.detail: The PR is titled as a mmengine/setuptools fix but also bumps mmdet a minor version. That's a second unrelated change riding along. If 3.3.0 is required for compatibility with mmengine 0.10.7 or mmcv 2.1.0, state it in a comment. Otherwise split it into its own commit so it can be bisected.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation silently couples mmcv build to the ambient setuptools.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv now reads whatever setuptools is in the active env. It works only because the preceding line pins setuptools<82, but the coupling is invisible. A one-line comment stating that mmcv must build against the env's setuptools<82 would save the next maintainer significant archaeology.

issues.description: FIXME comments lack a concrete revert condition or owner.
issues.detail: The FIXMEs point at mmcv#3325 but never state what flips the cap off (e.g., once mmcv ships a release that builds against setuptools>=82) or who owns checking. Six months on, someone greps FIXME and has to reverse-engineer the trigger. Add the explicit revert criterion.

issues.description: Three near-identical setuptools<82 pins exist with no shared source of truth.
issues.detail: env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py each independently assert setuptools<82 with overlapping FIXMEs pointing at the same upstream issue. When mmcv#3325 is resolved, three sites must be edited in sync. A shared constant or single script invite-point would let one edit fully revert the workaround.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a narrow, reasonable CI fix — pin setuptools<82 to dodge pkg_resources removal that breaks mmcv 2.1.0's build, and switch mmengine from a git SHA to PyPI 0.10.7. The dominant complaint is scope leak: the setuptools cap is duplicated into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, propagating a CI-only constraint to every downstream user. Secondary issues are an unexplained mmdet 3.2.0->3.3.0 bump bundled in, implicit coupling from --no-build-isolation, and FIXMEs that lack revert criteria. NEEDS-WORK but not wrong — split the unrelated changes and keep the workaround in CI.
